key_insight: This paper argues that text-to-image models can do more than generate pictures: their learned RGB priors can be repurposed as strong backbones for dense prediction tasks. The key shift is from "generating targets" in image space to directly reading out dense fields in pixel space.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between using generative text-to-image models for dense prediction and the true goal of predicting structured outputs like depth, normals, masks, alpha mattes, and heatmaps. Existing methods often force these outputs through an image-like latent representation, which can limit accuracy and flexibility.
method: Reinterpret text-to-image models as pixel-space dense prediction backbones instead of pure RGB generators.
Replace target-generation-style decoding with a dense field readout mechanism that predicts structured outputs directly from learned visual features.
Leverage the semantic, geometric, and structural priors already embedded in large-scale RGB pretraining to improve dense prediction performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new way to reuse foundation generative models for vision tasks beyond synthesis. It could reduce the need for task-specific architectures and improve dense prediction quality by exploiting pretrained priors more directly.

paper_title: From RGB Generation to Dense Field Readout: Pixel-Space Dense Prediction with Text-to-Image Models
paper_authors: Zanyi Wang, Xin Lin, Haodong Li, Dengyang Jiang, Yijiang Li
